content.thinking:
If notice was served by email on 10 October 2026, the two-month minimum period under the Act would run to 10 December 2026, and the tenancy can end on that specific date without needing to align with the rent period.

I should message the tenant confirming this date, request landlord approval noting the possibility of an earlier end date if they agree in writing, and schedule a follow-up for the checkout inspection around 10 December. I'll mention the deposit is protected with mydeposits and will be returned after checkout within the required timeframe, without inventing specifics about key return arrangements that haven't been confirmed yet.

arguments.body:
Hi Tom,

Thanks for letting us know, and congratulations on the new job. We've received your notice today (10 October 2026).

Under the current rules, tenants need to give at least two months' notice, so one month isn't enough on its own. The earliest your tenancy can end is 10 December 2026. Your rent stays payable until then. We've asked your landlord, Ben, whether he'd agree in writing to an earlier date such as 10 November. Only he can agree that, and until he confirms in writing, 10 December stands. We'll update you as soon as we hear.

Moving out: we're starting the process now. We'll arrange a checkout inspection around your end date and email you a time. Please hand all keys back at that checkout, or to us before then, and we'll confirm exactly how when we send the time. Please don't leave keys in the flat or post them without telling us.

Deposit: your £2,019 is protected with mydeposits. After checkout we'll compare the flat with the check-in condition. Any deductions are agreed with you, or decided by the scheme's free dispute service if we can't agree. The deposit is returned within 10 days of agreement.

We'll be in touch by 17 October with Ben's answer.

Kind regards,
Mare & Co Lettings

arguments.decision_needed: Tenant Tom Achterberg (Flat 2, 5 Navarino Road) gave notice on 10 Oct 2026 asking to leave on 10 Nov 2026 (new job in Manchester). Valid notice needs two months, so earliest end is 10 Dec 2026. Do you agree in writing to an earlier end date of 10 Nov? Steps already started: acknowledged to Tom, checkout inspection and key return being planned around the valid end date, deposit (£2,019, mydeposits) to be handled after checkout. Please reply by 14 Oct.
options: Keep 10 December 2026 as end date (default, no action needed)

arguments.purpose: Arrange checkout inspection and key return around tenancy end 10 Dec 2026 (or earlier date if landlord agrees in writing); give tenant 24h+ notice of time; then deposit return via mydeposits.
Chase landlord on whether he accepts earlier end date of 10 Nov; update tenant by 17 Oct.

content.thinking:
If notice was served by email on 10 October 2026, the two-month minimum period under the Act would run to 10 December 2026, and the tenancy can end on that specific date without needing to align with the rent period.

I should message the tenant confirming this date, request landlord approval noting the possibility of an earlier end date if they agree in writing, and schedule a follow-up for the checkout inspection around 10 December. I'll mention the deposit is protected with mydeposits and will be returned after checkout within the required timeframe, without inventing specifics about key return arrangements that haven't been confirmed yet.

arguments.body:
Hi Tom,

Thanks for letting us know, and congratulations on the new job. We've received your notice today (10 October 2026).

Under the current rules, tenants need to give at least two months' notice, so one month isn't enough on its own. The earliest your tenancy can end is 10 December 2026. Your rent stays payable until then. We've asked your landlord, Ben, whether he'd agree in writing to an earlier date such as 10 November. Only he can agree that, and until he confirms in writing, 10 December stands. We'll update you as soon as we hear.

Moving out: we're starting the process now. We'll arrange a checkout inspection around your end date and email you a time. Please hand all keys back at that checkout, or to us before then, and we'll confirm exactly how when we send the time. Please don't leave keys in the flat or post them without telling us.

Deposit: your £2,019 is protected with mydeposits. After checkout we'll compare the flat with the check-in condition. Any deductions are agreed with you, or decided by the scheme's free dispute service if we can't agree. The deposit is returned within 10 days of agreement.

We'll be in touch by 17 October with Ben's answer.

Kind regards,
Mare & Co Lettings

arguments.decision_needed: Tenant Tom Achterberg (Flat 2, 5 Navarino Road) gave notice on 10 Oct 2026 asking to leave on 10 Nov 2026 (new job in Manchester). Valid notice needs two months, so earliest end is 10 Dec 2026. Do you agree in writing to an earlier end date of 10 Nov? Steps already started: acknowledged to Tom, checkout inspection and key return being planned around the valid end date, deposit (£2,019, mydeposits) to be handled after checkout. Please reply by 14 Oct.
options: Keep 10 December 2026 as end date (default, no action needed)

arguments.purpose: Arrange checkout inspection and key return around tenancy end 10 Dec 2026 (or earlier date if landlord agrees in writing); give tenant 24h+ notice of time; then deposit return via mydeposits.
Chase landlord on whether he accepts earlier end date of 10 Nov; update tenant by 17 Oct.
